verdict: OK to lend in Aurangabad two-wheelers, but only to suppliers and dealers tied to the Ather Aurangabad plant ramp and to established ICE dealers; avoid pure EV-retail bets and single-OEM component shops until the plant's ramp is visible.
title: Aurangabad two-wheelers: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Aurangabad's two-wheeler story is now a plant story, not a showroom story.** The city hosts Ather Energy's new factory, scheduled to go live by end-December 2026, with Phase 1 adding five lakh units of annual capacity and a ramp to 40,000-42,000 scooters a month over about two quarters [1]. Around it sit component feeders, logistics, dealer floors and charging/after-sales. Cash is made on throughput and inventory turns, not on price: OEMs hold pricing power, suppliers and dealers absorb cost swings. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower's cash comes from Ather's ramp or from retail walk-ins; if it is the latter, ask for the last six months of unit sales.**

## What has changed now
**Demand is running ahead of supply, which is a good problem for the plant and a bad one for dealers.** Ather's waiting periods crossed four months, dealers in several states paused fresh orders, and 1.5 lakh paid preorders (Rs 2,500 deposit) came in the April-June quarter against roughly 90,000 retail registrations [1]. The company itself says the gap is wider than its usual 20% preorder drop-off [1]. Peer results confirm the cycle: industry sales grew 27 percent in Q2, with Bajaj, TVS and Hero posting strong revenue and profit [4], and Hero's market share climbed to 7.3% on scooters and VIDA EVs [6]. **The risk is not demand; it is execution timing of the Aurangabad ramp and input-cost inflation, which Hero flagged even as volumes grew [7].**

## Where to grow
**Pursue the plant's supplier and service ecosystem first.** Component and sub-assembly vendors selling to the Aurangabad OEM line have short working-capital cycles because OEMs pay promptly under just-in-time procurement [10]; that is the cleanest lending in this city. Second, established multi-brand dealers with ICE plus EV mix and audited stock statements. Third, logistics and warehousing tied to Phase 1 volumes [1]. **Avoid single-customer EV-only retail showrooms and anyone whose business case is the Phase 2 line, since investment there has not begun [1].**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the ramp, not the press release.** For supplier loans, take monthly dispatch volumes to the Aurangabad plant, OEM purchase orders and receivables ageing; for dealers, monthly stock and sales statements and floor-plan inventory counts. Covenant on debt-service cover and limit utilisation, since efficient working-capital management and lower bank-limit utilisation are explicit rating upgrade factors [11]. **Take every month: GST returns, bank statements, unit-wise sales, and OEM order book.** Note the data pack shows bank credit growing 27.0% against output of 22.7% [D] — credit is running ahead of production, so ask what the extra borrowing is funding.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the ramp, not the headlines.** If Ather's Aurangabad go-live slips past December 2026 or monthly output stays below the 40,000-42,000 target beyond two quarters [1], freeze new supplier limits. If a dealer's bookings pause extends or preorder cancellations exceed the usual 20% [1], cut floor-plan exposure. If input-cost pressure compresses a borrower's margin the way it did Hero's [7], reprice or ask for hedging policy, which ICRA treats as central to 2W analysis [8]. **Local Aurangabad-specific sales data is thin in these sources; lean on the plant timeline and peer results until you collect city-level registration data from the customer.**
watch: Ather Aurangabad output below 40,000-42,000/month beyond two quarters [1] -> freeze new supplier limits
Preorder drop-off above the usual 20% [1] -> cut floor-plan exposure
GST turnover falling while borrowing rises -> ask for funding use, tighten limit
OEM purchase orders and receivables ageing (monthly)
Receivables ageing beyond agreed terms -> demand escrow or reduce limit
Margin compression like Hero's [7] -> reprice or require hedging policy [8]
